f3_program: collection("keiko.sent_text_messages", "text_message", "keiko", source("Keiko sent 111 text messages last week"))
observe(at("keiko.sent_text_messages.count", "last_week"), 111, "count", source("Keiko sent 111 text messages last week"))

offset(at("keiko.sent_text_messages.count", "this_week"), scale(at("keiko.sent_text_messages.count", "last_week"), 2), -50, "count", source("This week she sent 50 less than double what she sent last week"))
query("sum", "keiko.sent_text_messages", "last_week_and_this_week")
collection("small_zoo.animals", "animal", "small_zoo", source("A small zoo houses a variety of 68 wild animals"))
observe(at("small_zoo.animals.count", "initial"), 68, "count", source("A small zoo houses a variety of 68 wild animals"))
transfer("send_gorilla_family", "small_zoo", at("small_zoo.animals.count", "current"), at("different_zoo.animals.count", "current"), 6, source("they send a gorilla family of six to a different zoo"))
transfer("adopt_hippopotamus", "small_zoo", at("another_zoo.animals.count", "current"), at("small_zoo.animals.count", "current"), 1, source("they adopt a hippopotamus from another zoo"))

transfer("take_in_rhinos", "small_zoo", at("animal_rescue.animals.count", "current"), at("small_zoo.animals.count", "current"), 3, source("an animal rescue contacted them, and the zoo took in three endangered rhinos"))
produce("lion_cub_birth", "small_zoo.lioness", at("small_zoo.animals.count", "current"), "small_zoo.lion_cubs.born.count", source("one of their lionesses gave birth to cubs"))

add("open_meerkat_exhibit", "small_zoo", at("small_zoo.animals.count", "current"), scale(event_field("lion_cub_birth", "quantity"), 2), source("they opened a meerkat exhibit with twice as many meerkats as they had gained lion cubs"))
observe(at("small_zoo.animals.count", "then"), 90, "count", source("The zoo then had 90 animals in all"))
query("value", event_field("lion_cub_birth", "quantity"))
assumptions: Opening the meerkat exhibit adds its meerkats to the zoo's animal count.

f3_program: collection("mary.story.characters", "character", "mary.story", source("her 60 characters"))
observe(at("mary.story.characters.count", "current"), 60, "count", source("60 characters"))
fraction_of(at("mary.story.characters.initial_a.count", "current"), at("mary.story.characters.count", "current"), 1, 2, source("Half of her characters have the initial A"))
fraction_of(at("mary.story.characters.initial_c.count", "current"), at("mary.story.characters.initial_a.count", "current"), 1, 2, source("half of this amount have the initial C"))

sum_relation(at("mary.story.characters.count", "current"), at("mary.story.characters.initial_a.count", "current"), at("mary.story.characters.initial_c.count", "current"), at("mary.story.characters.initial_d.count", "current"), at("mary.story.characters.initial_e.count", "current"), source("Half of her characters have the initial A, and half of this amount have the initial C. Mary wants the rest of her characters to have the initials D and E"))

multiple(at("mary.story.characters.initial_d.count", "current"), at("mary.story.characters.initial_e.count", "current"), 2, source("twice as many characters with the initial D as there are characters with the initial E"))
query("value", at("mary.story.characters.initial_d.count", "current"))
collection("pete.books_read", "book", "pete", source("Pete read twice as many books as Matt did last year"))
collection("matt.books_read", "book", "matt", source("Matt read 75 books in his second year"))
multiple(at("pete.books_read.count", "last_year"), at("matt.books_read.count", "last_year"), 2, source("Pete read twice as many books as Matt did last year"))
multiple(at("pete.books_read.count", "this_year"), at("pete.books_read.count", "last_year"), 2, source("this year he doubles that number"))
percent_more(at("matt.books_read.count", "this_year"), at("matt.books_read.count", "last_year"), 50, source("Matt reads only 50% more"))
observe(at("matt.books_read.count", "this_year"), 75, "count", source("Matt read 75 books in his second year"))
query("sum", "pete.books_read", "both_years")
assumptions: “he” and “that number” refer to Pete and Pete's last-year book count; Matt's “second year” is this year.

f3_program: observe(at("marianne.age", "when_bella_was_8"), 20, "year", source("Marianne was 20 years old"))
observe(at("bella.age", "when_bella_was_8"), 8, "year", source("Bella was 8 years old"))
observe(at("bella.age", "when_bella_turns_18"), 18, "year", source("Bella turns 18"))
query("value", at("marianne.age", "when_bella_turns_18"))
